question: Determine the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$ for which $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&x+1&2y-1\\3x-5&4&z+2\\y+3&2z-1&6\end{bmatrix}$$ is symmetric, and hence verify for the resulting matrix that $A+A'=2A$.
explanation:
Required Condition

For a symmetric matrix, $A'=A$, so corresponding entries on opposite sides of the principal diagonal must be equal. Therefore, $$x+1=3x-5$$ which gives $2x=6$, hence $x=3$. Also, $$2y-1=y+3$$ gives $y=4$, and $$z+2=2z-1$$ gives $z=3$.

Substituting the obtained values, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&4&7\\4&4&5\\7&5&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Since $$A'=\begin{bmatrix}2&4&7\\4&4&5\\7&5&6\end{bmatrix}=A,$$ the matrix is symmetric.

Verification

Now, $$A+A'=\begin{bmatrix}2&4&7\\4&4&5\\7&5&6\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2&4&7\\4&4&5\\7&5&6\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}4&8&14\\8&8&10\\14&10&12\end{bmatrix}$$ On the other hand, $$2A=2\begin{bmatrix}2&4&7\\4&4&5\\7&5&6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4&8&14\\8&8&10\\14&10&12\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $A+A'=2A$, and the required values are $x=3$, $y=4$ and $z=3$.
